template_rule: Only exact owned fixture URL and credential-file parameters replaced; expected newline generated for capture platform. Actual streams remain raw.

cases.stderr_lf_template: [shim] note: the daemon at {fixture_url} reports status=degraded (db: synthetic unavailable)

[shim] the daemon at {fixture_url} requires bearer authentication (/health reports auth=true) and this shim has no credential configured — every call would be rejected with 401.
  Give the MCP registration one of these in its env block:
    PSEUDOLIFE_MCP_TOKEN_FILE=<absolute path to a private file holding the token>   (preferred; reloaded per call)
    PSEUDOLIFE_MCP_TOKEN=<the token>
  Claude Desktop launches MCP servers with a sanitized environment, so a token exported in the OS env (setx / shell profile) does NOT reach it — the entry in claude_desktop_config.json must carry the setting itself (ops/install.* --client claude-desktop writes it; then fully quit and relaunch Desktop).

[shim] this shim is pseudolife-mcp 0.16.1 but the daemon at {fixture_url} is 99.0.0 — run pseudolife-mcp update --clients-only --tag 99.0.0 (installs the daemon's release as a new shim runtime beside this one and refreshes the plugin cache; from a checkout: python ops/update_clients.py --only shim), or update the daemon (pseudolife-mcp update); then start a new session.

[shim] the daemon at {fixture_url} is up but refusing to serve:
  synthetic initialization refusal

[shim] no daemon at {fixture_url} and PSEUDOLIFE_MCP_NO_SPAWN is set — waiting up to 5s for it instead of spawning a fallback (Docker may still be starting)...
[shim] no answer from the memory daemon at {fixture_url}.
  (PSEUDOLIFE_MCP_NO_SPAWN is set, so no fallback daemon was spawned.)
  Docker tier:  docker compose -f ops/docker-compose.yml up -d
  Pip tiers:    pseudolife-mcp serve   (run it in a terminal — the daemon logs to its own stderr, so this shows why it died)
  This session starts without it: the shim serves the last tool list it
  saw from that daemon, retries the daemon on every call and in the
  background, and has the client re-list tools once it answers.

[shim] no daemon answering at {fixture_url} (another machine) — waiting up to 5s for it; this shim never starts a local daemon for a remote URL...
[shim] no answer from the memory daemon at {fixture_url}.
  That address is another machine, so no local daemon was started:
  a daemon spawned here could never be that one.
  Check the link to the daemon host (tailnet up? LAN route?), that
  the host exposes the port to this machine (e.g. `tailscale serve status` there), and that the daemon is running there (GET /health).
  This session starts without it: the shim serves the last tool list it
  saw from that daemon, retries the daemon on every call and in the
  background, and has the client re-list tools once it answers.
